principle: A nonexistent original is generated by fabricating the complete machinery of its recovery, where dense documented transmission substitutes for the source itself and the deliberately undocumented final link keeps the promised original permanently suspended beyond verification.

nodes.label: Found-manuscript frame with amputated recovery link
nodes.description: The narrative is presented as an edited translation of a recovered codex, with every internal transmission link documented except the final link to the modern editor, which is deliberately omitted. The frame terminates in a void rather than a recovery narrative.
evidence: Prologue and the Note on the Shire Records present the text as an edited translation of a recovered codex
Unlike Otranto or Cide Hamete conventions, the chain from Middle-earth to the modern editor is never narrated
Stage 4 validation: the Red Book is this frame; remove it and no work remains, since there is no freestanding text beneath the device
rules: Every internal transmission boundary is documented; only the terminal link to the modern editor is withheld

nodes.label: Layered composite authorship
nodes.description: The text is attributed in dated strata to Bilbo, Frodo, Sam, and later scribes, with visible seams such as crossed-out titles and blank final leaves reserved for a successor hand. Authorship is serialized, not unified.
evidence: Explicit attribution of strata: Bilbo memoir, Frodo continuation, Sam additions, Bilbo three volumes of Elvish translations
Diegetic composition scenes in The Grey Havens show the manuscript being handed between authors
Stage 4 validation: serialized strata make this a codex rather than a generic frame-tale; palimpsest, open edge, and errata absorption hang off it
rules: Narrative perspective is limited to attributed eyewitness hobbit testimony

nodes.label: Translation-layer disguise
nodes.description: Appendix F declares the English surface a systematic substitution for invented source languages, with Westron rendered as English and Rohirric as Old English, so the reader is told the shown text is never the original.
evidence: Appendix F specifies systematic linguistic substitution: Westron as English, Rohirric as Old English, hobbit names anglicized
Stage 4 validation: removal collapses nomenclature logic and reduces the appendices to trivia per the subtraction test
The declaration is a systematic specification, not an aside
rules: Every word of the surface text is a systematic substitution for a source language, never the original

nodes.label: Pseudo-editorial apparatus
nodes.description: Appendices A-F, dual calendar systems, genealogical tables, the Tale of Years, and translator footnotes form a scholarly armature attached to the narrative, supplying the checkable substrate the translation claim requires.
evidence: Appendices A-F, dual calendars in Appendix D, the Tale of Years in Appendix B, genealogical tables, translator footnotes
Stage 4 validation: co-dependent with the translation layer, though a thinner armature might arguably suffice; density rather than existence is the questionable part

nodes.label: Transmission stemma as fabricated patina
nodes.description: The Note on the Shire Records specifies copies, recensions, and interpolations: the Thains Book, Findegils Minas Tirith copy, later additions, annotations in multiple hands. Simulated wear and variance function as fabricated manuscript aging.
evidence: Specified copies and recensions: Thains Book, Findegils copy, the tale of Aragorn and Arwen added later, annotations in multiple hands
Stage 4 validation: amplifies authentication and makes the amputated final link legible as void; a simpler provenance chain could functionally substitute

nodes.label: Errata absorption
nodes.description: The discrepancy between the 1937 and 1951 versions of the riddle-game chapter is reconciled diegetically: Bilbos lie is recorded as the original entry, corrected in later recensions. Real-world revision is converted into fictional manuscript variance.
evidence: The riddle-game discrepancy between editions is reconciled as Bilbos recorded lie corrected in later recensions
Stage 4 validation: brilliant but opportunistic, exploiting a single real-world instance; the frame stands without it
rule_violations: Provenance apparatus conventionally certifies witness reliability rather than documenting the witness committing perjury

nodes.label: Open-edge incompleteness
nodes.description: Frodo leaves the final pages blank for Sam, making the manuscript terminal boundary an open edge that is structurally unfinished by design. The blank leaves enact the theme of succession as apparatus.
evidence: Frodo tells Sam the last pages are for him; the codex ends in reserved blank leaves
Stage 2: the frame open edge is not decoration around the ending; it is the ending mechanism
Stage 4 validation: converts the ending into apparatus, but the frame identity survives its removal
rules: The terminal boundary of the codex remains unwritten, reserved for a successor hand

nodes.label: Appendix F, On Translation
nodes.description: The concrete appendix declaring systematic linguistic substitution: Westron rendered as English, Rohirric as Old English, hobbit nomenclature anglicized.
evidence: Appendix F specifies the substitution scheme explicitly and systematically

nodes.label: Note on the Shire Records
nodes.description: The prologue section specifying the manuscript stemma: the Thains Book, Findegils copy, interpolations, and annotations in multiple hands.
evidence: Specifies copies, recensions, and interpolations with scribal precision

nodes.label: Undocumented terminal transmission link
nodes.description: The specified void between the Fourth Age copies and the modern editor: the one transmission boundary the apparatus deliberately refuses to document.
evidence: Every internal link in the stemma is documented; the final link is deliberately absent
Stage 2: exhaustive specification everywhere else is what makes the terminal void read as void rather than omission

nodes.label: Title-page palimpsest
nodes.description: In The Grey Havens, the manuscript title page displays crossed-out serial titles before Frodos final title, rendering revision history visible at the work boundary.
evidence: Crossed-out titles from My Diary through There and Back Again to Frodos final title are shown diegetically
Stage 4 validation: single-instance flourish; stratum boundaries are already established by explicit attribution elsewhere

nodes.label: Blank final leaves reserved for Sam
nodes.description: The concrete unwritten pages at the end of the codex, explicitly reserved by Frodo for Sam as the next contributing hand.
evidence: Frodo says the last pages are for Sam; the blank leaves are specified, not accidental negative space

nodes.label: Riddle-game textual variant
nodes.description: The real discrepancy between the 1937 and 1951 versions of the riddle-game chapter, the single actual variant the fiction absorbs as manuscript recension history.
evidence: The 1937 and 1951 versions differ; the fiction records Bilbos lie as the original entry corrected in later recensions

nodes.label: Verse with English rhyme, meter, and wordplay
nodes.description: Songs and poems whose rhyme, meter, and puns operate by aesthetic self-sufficiency in English and therefore cannot literally be translations of Westron originals.
evidence: Stage 3: English rhyme, meter, and puns cannot be translations; these passages operate inside a system claiming total derivativeness
Stage 3: strip the verbal pleasure to honor the conceit and the text fails as literature
rule_violations: Every word of the surface text is a systematic substitution for a source language, never the original

nodes.label: Scenes beyond hobbit testimony
nodes.description: Passages narrating Gollums private deliberations, councils no hobbit attended, and Boromirs death from perspectives no attributed witness could reach.
evidence: Stage 3: a codex attributed to eyewitness hobbits narrates private deliberations and deaths without survivors
Stage 3: the apparatus patches some breaches via debriefings and secondhand accounts but not all
rule_violations: Narrative perspective is limited to attributed eyewitness hobbit testimony

nodes.label: Appendix B, the Tale of Years
nodes.description: The annalistic chronology that narrates past the blank final leaves, documenting Sams departure and the end of the age within the same binding.
evidence: Stage 3: the blank leaves promise open succession, yet Appendix B narrates past them, closing the open edge elsewhere in the same binding

edges.rationale: The translation conceit requires the appendical apparatus to supply an original substrate; without the calendars, genealogies, and nomenclature tables the translation claim has no referent.
Remove the translation conceit and the appendices become trivia; each makes the other checkable, and each becomes inert without the other.
The attributed strata are strata of the recovered codex the frame posits; per progressive stripping, remove the frame and nothing remains for authorship to be serialized within.
Producing the original would make the frame falsifiable, so authentication depends on verification being permanently deferred one stratum beyond reach; the withheld link is what suspends the promise.

The amputated terminal link reads as active void only if all internal transmission links are documented with exhaustive scribal precision; density of documented links makes the single undocumented link conspicuous.
The stemma of copies, recensions, and interpolations supplies the provenance warrant the recovered-manuscript claim trades on, amplifying authentication with fabricated patina.
The stemma is concretely instantiated in the Note on the Shire Records, which specifies the Thains Book, Findegils copy, and later interpolations.
Errata absorption requires the transmission stemma to pre-establish the category of manuscript variance, otherwise the reconciliation is an ad hoc patch.
Without an actual variant to absorb, the stemma would be inert texture; the riddle-game deposit gives the variance category a real instance, though the stemma survives its removal.
The mechanism operates on exactly one concrete real-world discrepancy, the 1937 versus 1951 riddle-game chapter; without that variant there is nothing to absorb.
Recording Bilbos lie as an original entry corrected in later recensions makes the discrepancy proof of the manuscript existence, validating the frame by convicting its own witness.
The title-page palimpsest carries load only because composite authorship already serializes the text into attributed strata; crossed-out titles are legible as stratum boundaries, not decoration.
Blank final leaves carry load only because composite authorship serializes the text into attributed strata, so the leaves read as the next stratum awaiting deposit rather than narrative failure.
A title page displaying successive hands establishes the precedent that permits the blank leaves to read as succession; the open edge survives without it since attribution is established elsewhere.
Open-edge incompleteness is concretely instantiated by the blank leaves Frodo reserves for Sam; without them the terminal boundary is simply closed.
If apparatus density decreases below narrative need, the frame reverts to decoration and the documented feel of the world degrades; density strengthens the frame but the frame survives thinning.
The translation disguise is declared in Appendix F, its sole systematic specification; without that declaration the surface language is simply English, not a substitution.

If the translation claim is enforced on the verse, its rhyme, meter, and wordplay become impossible, so the frame must tolerate untranslated aesthetic self-sufficiency inside a system claiming total derivativeness.
The eyewitness memoir contract limits admissible perspective, and every scene beyond hobbit testimony strains the frame it cannot fully patch; the violation is systematic.
The open-edge promise of unwritten succession is contradicted by Appendix B, which narrates past the blank leaves within the same binding, closing the edge the codex claims to leave open.

violated: Narrative perspective is limited to attributed eyewitness hobbit testimony

failure_modes.consequence: The memoir frame breaks whenever the prose narrates scenes no attributed witness could access, such as private deliberations and deaths without survivors; the frame survives only by not pressing its own evidentiary standard.

If the terminal link is documented or the original demanded, the frame becomes falsifiable and the authentication loop collapses, since every checkable claim terminates in fabricated evidence; the circular apparatus fails exactly as Ossian did under Johnson.

violated: Every word of the surface text is a systematic substitution for a source language, never the original

failure_modes.consequence: The verse contradicts the total-derivativeness claim, since English rhyme and puns cannot be translations, forcing the frame to conceal a load-bearing exception; enforcing the rule would destroy the text as literature.

violated: The terminal boundary of the codex remains unwritten, reserved for a successor hand

failure_modes.consequence: The open-edge promise of unwritten succession is contradicted by Appendix B, which narrates past the blank leaves within the same binding; the codex simultaneously withholds and delivers its continuation.

violated: Provenance apparatus conventionally certifies witness reliability rather than documenting the witness committing perjury

failure_modes.consequence: Reliability is manufactured from documented unreliability: the frame convicts its own witness of lying in order to prove the manuscript exists, inverting the conventional purpose of provenance.
Since the Red Book has no existence apart from the frame apparatus, removing the found-manuscript frame leaves no work at all; there is no freestanding text beneath the device.

Without the appendical apparatus the translation claim loses its checkable substrate and referent, the nomenclature logic dangles, and the documented feel degrades toward decoration; the co-dependent pair fails together.

Without the documented internal stemma, the amputated terminal link stops reading as active void and reverts to mere omission, and errata absorption loses the pre-established category of manuscript variance, becoming an ad hoc patch.

asserted_removal_tests.M1: If removed, no work remains at all, since there is no freestanding text beneath the frame device.
asserted_removal_tests.M2: If removed, the codex collapses into a generic frame-tale and the palimpsest, open-edge ending, and errata absorption lose their attachment points.
asserted_removal_tests.M3: If removed, the nomenclature logic collapses and the appendices become inert trivia with no original substrate to reference.
asserted_removal_tests.M4: If removed, the translation claim loses its referent and the fabricated provenance becomes an unverifiable assertion rather than a simulated evidence system.
asserted_removal_tests.M5: If removed, the amputated final link stops reading as active void and errata lose their variance category; a simpler provenance chain could only partly substitute.
asserted_removal_tests.M6: If removed, the frame stands; what is lost is the opportunistic conversion of one real revision into fictional recension evidence.
asserted_removal_tests.M7: If removed, the frame identity survives, but the ending loses its formal enactment of succession as unwritten pages.
